items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I didn’t even see Sonny Payne or nobody.

ctx.x: Not a bottle or two, but a case.

Well you know actually I mean okay when I first heard about Joe Williams, everybody was talking about his singing you know, with Count Basie’s band. You know I mean at like Birdland you know? And at that time, I still am you know, I was a big fan of like © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Basie’s band you understand what I’m saying? And so and I mean I find myself okay now I went to Birdland, I found myself just being oogle-eyed at Joe Williams. I didn’t see the trombone player, I didn’t even see Sonny Payne or nobody. The man was fantastic. And as like he said, he’s a smart man, I mean because he didn’t have, or ask for, to my knowledge, he had never had a hit record on his own. So and like “Every Day” you know he give up to somebody else, and he’s still stepping. You understand what I’m saying?…
